Decoding the hex argument: `696D706F7274207074793B7074792E737061776E28222F62696E2F626173682229` translates to `import pty;pty.spawn("/bin/bash")`. This is a classic reverse-shell / TTY upgrade pattern: a Python one-liner spawning an interactive bash shell as root, with no legitimate administrative context visible. The process chain (python3 with -c, then bash with a pts1 tty allocated, parent PID 17398) is characteristic of an attacker who has gained command execution and is stabilizing an interactive shell.
